subject: paper:moffitt-2015-dunedin
quote: Unexpectedly, the childhood-ADHD and adult-ADHD groups comprised virtually non-overlapping sets; 90% of adult-ADHD cases lacked a history of childhood ADHD. Also unexpectedly, the adult-ADHD group did not show tested neuropsychological deficits in childhood or adulthood, nor did they show polygenic risk for childhood ADHD.
rationale: Verified against the PMC author manuscript. The strongest evidence AGAINST the late-identification reading — if adult cases carried childhood ADHD's polygenic risk, masking would predict it; they did not.

subject: paper:agnew-blais-2016
quote: Among 166 individuals with adult ADHD, 112 (67.5%) did not meet criteria for ADHD at any assessment in childhood.
rationale: Verified against the JAMA Psychiatry full article; independent cohort replicating the non-overlap finding that the late-identification hypothesis must explain away.

subject: paper:caye-2016-pelotas
quote: The findings of this study do not support the assumption that adulthood ADHD is necessarily a continuation of childhood ADHD. Rather, they suggest the existence of 2 syndromes that have distinct developmental trajectories.
rationale: Verified full article; the explicit two-syndromes alternative, kept live as the rival reading in tension:late-onset-vs-late-identification.

subject: paper:sibley-2018-late-onset
quote: Since symptoms were likely present but mitigated in childhood, these individuals might better be characterized as late-identified, rather than late-onset, ADHD cases
rationale: Verified against psychiatryonline full text; the reframing this notebook adopts, grounded in cases with above-average childhood symptoms and superior IQ.

subject: paper:sibley-2018-late-onset
quote: approximately 95% of case subjects who initially screened positive for late-onset ADHD were excluded from diagnosis
rationale: Verified full text; screening positive is a weak signal at cohort scale — most exclusions were because symptoms were better explained by substance use or another disorder. The mimic problem at population scale.

subject: paper:sibley-2022-remission
quote: Only 9.1% of the children with ADHD demonstrated recovery from ADHD (i.e., sustained remission to study endpoint; mean age, 25 years) and only 10.8% demonstrated stable ADHD persistence across all time points. For most of the sample (63.8%), the follow-up period was characterized by fluctuating persistence and remission (full or partial) in the absence of recovery.
rationale: Verified full text; refutes the persist/remit dichotomy and grounds person-environment fit as the evaluative frame.

subject: paper:staley-2024-mmwr
quote: In 2023, an estimated 15.5 million U.S. adults (6.0%) had a current ADHD diagnosis based on self-report; approximately one half received the diagnosis at age >=18 years.
rationale: Verified against the CDC MMWR page. Establishes that adult identification is the majority pathway, so absence of a childhood diagnosis is weak evidence against ADHD. Note: '>=' substituted for the source's typographic symbol.

subject: paper:song-2021-prevalence
quote: By adjusting for the global demographic structure in 2020, the prevalence of persistent adult ADHD was 2.58% and that of symptomatic adult ADHD was 6.76%
rationale: Verified against the fetched PDF; a 2.6x prevalence swing driven purely by whether childhood onset is required — definitional, not empirical.

subject: paper:matte-2015-field-trial
quote: Our results, combined with previous findings, suggest a 27% increase in the expected prevalence of ADHD among young adults, comparing DSM-IV to DSM-5 criteria.
rationale: Verified via Cambridge Core; quantifies how much a threshold change alone moves prevalence.

subject: paper:mowlem-2019-sex
quote: Among these children, 303 (18.5%) of the males with elevated symptoms, and 111 (12.1%) of the females with elevated symptoms had an ADHD diagnosis recorded in the NPR.
rationale: Verified against the open-access PDF; same population and symptom level, different diagnosis rate — the filter is the diagnostic pathway, not the trait.

subject: paper:mowlem-2019-sex
quote: These results may also suggest that externalising behaviours drive referral for ADHD, speaking to the view that externalising behaviours are more likely to get females clinical recognition for their symptoms.
rationale: Verified full-text PDF; identifies the specific mechanism of the ascertainment filter.

subject: paper:hinshaw-2022-girls
quote: Second, even in representative samples, the sex ratio of diagnosed ADHD approaches 1.5:1 or lower during the adult years (Kessler et al., 2006; Nussbaum, 2012).
rationale: Verified against the APSARD-hosted PDF; a childhood ratio that converges in adulthood is the signature of under-detection rather than true prevalence difference.

subject: paper:hinshaw-2022-girls
quote: As well, symptom lists for ADHD are biased toward male behaviors (e.g., physical overactivity or extreme risk-taking) as opposed to female-related manifestations (e.g., excessive verbalizations or more subtle indicators of impulsivity; see Quinn & Madhoo, 2014; Young et al., 2020).
rationale: Verified full-text PDF; the instrument itself carries a reference-sample bias, another reason a single rating score is a weak anchor.

subject: paper:willcutt-2012-prevalence
quote: Analyses of diagnostic subtypes indicated that the predominantly inattentive type is the most common subtype in the population, but individuals with the combined type are more likely to be referred for clinical services.
rationale: Verified against the Springer abstract; the structural referral filter that removes quiet presentations regardless of sex.

subject: paper:metin-2013
quote: The arousal and activation are affected from a number of external and internal factors, such as availability of environmental stimulation, stress, sleep-wake cycle, noise, and, medications.
rationale: Verified against the Ghent dissertation PDF (sic on 'affected from'). The energetic pools are defined as sleep- and stress-sensitive, so the mimics move the same variable by construction — the basis for the confounds edges.

subject: paper:isaac-2023-arousal
quote: the underlying impairment in ADHD is associated with the ability to self-regulate arousal rather than having a constant under or over aroused physiological state
rationale: Verified against Frontiers full text; locates the putatively ADHD-specific element in regulation rather than level. Medium because the same authors note the evidence 'continue[s] to show mixed results'.

subject: paper:sergeant-2005-cem
quote: Increasing evidence suggests that inhibition deficits associated with ADHD may, at least in part, be explained in terms of an energetic dysfunction.
rationale: Verified via PubMed abstract; positions state regulation upstream of the inhibition findings. Medium because the same abstract concedes the model needs direct measures of the energetic pools.

subject: paper:bozhilova-2018-mw
quote: We propose that altered deactivation of the default mode network, and dysfunctional interaction with the executive control network, leads to excessive and spontaneous MW, which underpins symptoms and impairments of ADHD.
rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the mechanistic proposal defining the mind-wandering axis.

subject: paper:mowlem-2019-mews
quote: Furthermore, the contribution of MW to impairment was independent of the core ADHD symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity. These findings suggest that excessive MW is a characteristic feature of adult ADHD that has specific effects on impairment.
rationale: Verified against the Sage PDF. Medium because the increment was small in the comorbidity-free sample (R2 delta = .024) and much larger only where anxiety/depression co-occurred.

subject: paper:figueiredo-2020-mw
quote: Our results suggest MW is associated with anxiety levels, independently of an ADHD diagnosis.
rationale: Verified against the author-hosted PDF; the specificity failure. Medium because the sample was small (n=78 adolescents) and underpowered.

subject: paper:figueiredo-2020-mw
quote: However, MW has been also associated with different developmental stages (Maillet et al., 2018), medication use (Raymond et al., 2019) and even Alzheimer's disease (El Haj et al., 2019) and cannot be considered a 'hallmark' of ADHD.
rationale: Verified full text; the explicit non-specificity claim against the mind-wandering mechanism.

subject: paper:hvolby-2015-sleep
quote: No experimental study has yet shown that sleep restriction induces hyperactivity, impulsivity or externalizing behaviors in children (Beebe 2011), despite the perception that 'paradoxical' hyperactivity exists as a behavioral response to daytime sleepiness
rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the boundary that narrows the sleep rival to the inattention half of the picture.

subject: paper:gruber-2012-sleep
quote: a cumulative restriction of sleep of 54.04 minutes was associated with detectable deterioration
rationale: Verified full text; experimental demonstration that modest sleep restriction degrades behaviour in children with no prior sleep or behavioural problems — the mimic shown causally.

subject: paper:alarachi-2024
quote: To differentiate between ADHD and clinical anxiety, assessors may benefit from specifically asking patients whether restlessness, problems relaxing, and feeling driven by a motor are still present in the absence of clinical anxiety symptoms or prior to onset of an anxiety or related disorder.
rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the counterfactual and temporal test — the concrete method for attacking tension:adhd-vs-anxiety-internal-restlessness.

subject: paper:alarachi-2024
quote: The ADHD item having difficulty unwinding or relaxing (item within the factor of Hyperactivity) demonstrated poor specificity with measures of generalized anxiety.
rationale: Verified full text; identifies the single worst-behaving item — and it is precisely an internal-restlessness item.

subject: paper:cortese-2025-adult-adhd
quote: a) consider the age of onset of the symptoms (for example, when disentangling inattention as part of ADHD versus a mild chronic depressive disorder, the occurrence of inattentive symptoms before the onset of any mood symptoms reinforces the ADHD diagnosis); b) examine the trajectory of the symptoms (for example, the clearly episodic occurrence of hyperactivity, impulsivity and irritability can suggest bipolar disorder); and c) assess if the way symptoms manifest is better explained by another mental disorder
rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the three structural tests generalised — onset, trajectory, mechanism.

subject: paper:cortese-2025-adult-adhd
quote: Thus, hyperactivity in adults often manifests as inner restlessness, overscheduling, or not being able to relax properly.
rationale: Verified full text; establishes that inner restlessness is a recognised adult manifestation of ADHD hyperactivity, so the personal hypothesis is at least well-formed. Medium and deliberately weak: this is a general clinical description, not evidence about this case, and the same mechanism has three standing confounds edges.

subject: paper:lipszyc-schachar-2010
quote: We found medium deficits in stop signal reaction time (SSRT), reflecting the speed of the inhibitory process, for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) (g = 0.62), obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) (g = 0.77) and schizophrenia (SCZ) (g = 0.69).
rationale: Verified via Europe PMC REST. OCD's inhibition deficit EXCEEDS ADHD's, so the stop-signal task cannot be an ADHD-specific marker — the strongest form of the non-specificity argument.
